note: Faithful rendering of the general/specific and direct/indirect characteristics of the four truths and the two kinds of those seeking liberation.

errors.english: Therefore, a single cognition does not possess multiple referents,
errors.why: The verse affirms that one (cognition) has many objects; the English inserts a negation and states the opposite of the author's conclusion.

fix.find: Therefore, a single cognition does not possess multiple referents,
fix.replace: Therefore, a single cognition possesses multiple referents,

errors.english: it would be logical to speak of a single referent inhering in them
errors.why: The point is ekārthasamavāya: the number 'manyness' (མང་པོའི་གྲངས་ཉིད, rendered loosely as 'an aggregate of many trees') and floweredness co-inhere in one and the same substrate, not that a single referent inheres in the trees.

note: Generally careful rendering of the citra-cognition argument, but the concluding root verse is negated, inverting the thesis.

errors.english: filled with beautiful light, which serves
errors.why: The city is white like camphor with the mass of light from its palaces/mansions (Skt. saudha); the mansions are dropped and the light made merely 'beautiful'.

note: Colophon and opening verses of the Maṇicūḍa chapter are rendered adequately, both in the Sanskrit gloss and the Tibetan version, with some freedom in the verse paraphrase.

errors.english: If they cover it with boards, there is no offense.
errors.why: སྤང་ལེབ are slabs of turf/sod, distinct from the wooden boards (ཤིང་ལེབ) of the next clause.

note: Sound rendering of the commentary on the vihāra-building pācattika, its conditions and the Upāliparipṛcchā citation.

errors.english: a plural word used with the intention of expressing clarity
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is vyakti, the individual instances; the plural is used to refer to the individuals, not to express 'clarity'.

fix.find: used with the intention of expressing clarity
fix.replace: used with the intention of expressing the individual instances (vyakti)

errors.english: the mental consciousness itself, which performs the connection,
errors.why: མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ is pratisandhi, rebirth-linking: the mental consciousness that links rebirth is the 'being'.

fix.find: the mental consciousness itself, which performs the connection,
fix.replace: the mental consciousness itself, which effects rebirth-linking (pratisandhi),

errors.english: If the support causes the destruction of staying by itself or through another
errors.why: The Tibetan is 'if the support brings about the staying of what perishes (whether from itself or from another)', not the destruction of staying.

errors.english: there is no reason for that functional thing to remain as a support
errors.why: The Tibetan says a cause of staying (sthitihetu) is purposeless for that thing; the thing is not said to remain as a support.

errors.english: the fuel (upādāna) appropriation or material cause and that which arises from the fuel—the light and the lamp—
errors.why: The pair is material cause and what arises from it, namely the lamp and its light; rendering upādāna as 'fuel' misidentifies the relata.

note: The argument against a support of mind is followed in outline, but several technical terms (vyakti, pratisandhi, upādāna) and the sthitihetu clauses are misread.

errors.english: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like, so that the individual may quickly "take up" the remedy and "separate" from the fault
errors.why: It is the pupil who must strive and help so that his preceptor/teacher quickly obtains the penance etc. from the Saṅgha and is quickly released; the Saṅgha is the source of the penance, not the helper.

fix.find: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like, so that the individual may quickly "take up" the remedy and "separate" from the fault
fix.replace: the pupil must exert himself and help so that the preceptor or teacher may quickly obtain the penance and the like from the Sangha and quickly be released from it

errors.english: the resident monk should not merely ask questions; he must also provide assistance
errors.why: The teacher of dependence is simply exempt from asking permission, but otherwise must render the same services (bowl, robes etc.) to the pupil; 'not merely ask questions' inverts the exemption.

fix.find: the resident monk should not merely ask questions; he must also provide assistance
fix.replace: the teacher of dependence, though he need not ask permission, must likewise provide assistance

errors.english: a fault of concealing a remaining offense (shispa) an offense requiring purification from the preceptor or the resident teacher
errors.why: ལྷག་མ here is a saṅghāvaśeṣa offense, concealed by the preceptor or teacher; 'remaining offense (shispa)' is not a Vinaya term and 'from the preceptor' blurs whose offense it is.

fix.find: a fault of concealing a remaining offense (shispa) an offense requiring purification from the preceptor or the resident teacher
fix.replace: a concealed saṅghāvaśeṣa offense on the part of the preceptor or the teacher of dependence

errors.english: If one wishes to remove [note: an offense or obstacle]
errors.why: དབྱུང་བ here closes the list of saṅghāvaśeṣa procedures (penance, probation, mānatva...): it is the rehabilitation (āvarhaṇa) of the offender, not removing an offense or obstacle.

note: The later passage on the ten-year rule and the four abilities is fine, but the opening on the pupil's duties toward a teacher under penance confuses roles and the saṅghāvaśeṣa procedure.

errors.english: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body
errors.why: The quoted formula says the Tathāgata's body is born from all wholesome qualities; that qualifier is dropped.

fix.find: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body
fix.replace: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone, born from all wholesome qualities, is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body

errors.english: Because they are the essential nature of what should and should not be done
errors.why: The etymology says that, being of the nature of action and non-action, they are karma, and being paths to good and bad destinies, they are paths: hence karmapatha; the 'they are karma' step is lost.

note: A clear, accurate rendering of the instructions for stabilizing faith, with one dropped qualifier in the quoted Dharmakāya formula.

errors.english: when it is stated that a part of the subject's property that is to be proven is pervaded
errors.why: The definition (pakṣadharmas tadaṃśena vyāptaḥ) is that the property of the subject is pervaded BY a part of the thesis (pakṣa), i.e. by the property to be proven; the English makes 'a part' the pervaded.

fix.find: when it is stated that a part of the subject's property that is to be proven is pervaded
fix.replace: when it is stated that the property of the subject of the thesis is pervaded by a part of the thesis (pakṣa)

errors.english: such a distinction is impossible
errors.why: The reason is that being present everywhere (in all instances) is impossible for a particular (viśeṣa), not that 'such a distinction' is impossible.

errors.english: it is appropriate that the qualifier itself functions as the means of understanding
errors.why: ཁྱད་པར་བྱ་བ is the qualified (viśeṣya), not the qualifier (ཁྱད་པར་བྱེད་པ); the distinction is the point of the three restrictions being discussed.

note: Follows the Hetubindu discussion of pervasion and the three restrictive particles in outline, but the core definition's case roles and the qualifier/qualified distinction are confused.

errors.english: possessing number is also impossible for them, because these two
errors.why: གྲངས་དང་ལྡན་པ is 'number and conjunction (saṃyoga)', the two Vaiśeṣika qualities that inhere only in substances, hence 'these two'.

fix.find: possessing number is also impossible for them, because these two
fix.replace: number and conjunction are also impossible for them, because these two

note: Careful and accurate rendering of the regress argument against space's qualities, with one mistaken Vaiśeṣika term.

errors.english: (sanghadisesa) rules requiring an assembly of the community
errors.why: Pali form in a Mūlasarvāstivāda text; the Sanskrit is saṅghāvaśeṣa (also in 'the thirteen (sanghadisesa) are recited').

fix.find: (sanghadisesa) rules requiring an assembly of the community
fix.replace: (saṅghāvaśeṣa) rules requiring an assembly of the community

errors.english: (uposatha) the bimonthly purification ritual
errors.why: Pali form where the Sanskrit tradition (poṣadha) is meant.

errors.english: This mental resolve is the blessing.
errors.why: བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབ་པ here is the Vinaya adhiṣṭhāna, a mental determination to remedy the offense later, not a 'blessing'.

note: Accurate account of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's and elder's duties, with Pali forms and one mistranslated Vinaya term.
